title: hello-channel — a Slack bot compiled into a daemon (target: channel)

beats.label: Open the starter README
beats.cue: “A spec in, a long-running daemon out — it listens for Slack webhooks and replies in-thread.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed crewhaus.yaml stays untouched.

beats.label: Load the credentials
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env for the boot beats — Anthropic plus the two Slack secrets.

verify.note: operator-supplied demos/.env; the Slack beats also want SLACK_BOT_TOKEN + SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET

groups.title: Beat 1 · The spec: a Slack bot in six blocks

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape
beats.cue: “Two lines: what it's called, and target: channel — the long-running daemon shape.”

beats.label: The agent — model and instructions
beats.cue: “You are a Slack bot… reply concisely (1-2 sentences) in the same thread.”

beats.label: Give it hands
beats.cue: Two hands: read the repo, run a shell. The gate on bash arrives later in the same file.

beats.label: Wire it to Slack
beats.cue: Slack is two env refs. No token ever lands in the spec — the compiler emits the lookup.

beats.label: Route a thread to a session
beats.cue: “sessionKey: thread — every Slack thread gets its own persistent session.”

beats.label: Fence the shell
beats.cue: Read auto-allowed, Bash(**) ask-gated — the policy ships in the spec, not in a review.

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “Parse plus the IR passes the compile path skips — nothing emitted yet.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “The spec is sugar; this JSON is the channel IR the compiler actually sees.”

verify.note: prints the IR for target channel (slack adapter, secret refs unresolved)

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots it: GREEN, with no token in the room.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (4 anchors); install ok; boot gated at the spec env refs gate

beats.label: Open the emitted gateway
beats.cue: One spec, five files. The gateway verifies the webhook signature before anything runs.

beats.label: Open the session router
beats.cue: sha256 of adapter:workspace:channel:thread → sess_<16hex>. Same thread, same session.

beats.label: Ask run to run it
beats.cue: “run is the cli/browser REPL. A daemon isn't a chat — the CLI names the shapes it takes.”

verify.note: deliberate rejection — `crewhaus run supports target: cli or browser (got "channel")`

beats.label: Boot the daemon with no secrets
beats.cue: “Strip the four secrets back out, and it names every env var it needs before it opens a socket — exit 2.”
beats.command: env -u SLACK_BOT_TOKEN -u SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET -u ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY bun live/dist/daemon.ts

verify.note: designed refusal — `[daemon] missing required env vars: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; deps installed by the --check beat. `env -u` makes it deterministic: the Setup group already sourced .env into this same terminal, and with those four present the daemon would boot and listen instead

beats.label: Give the webhook a public URL
beats.cue: “Use ngrok or similar for local dev” — the Request URL is that host + /slack/events. Run it in your own terminal, not this one: this terminal has beats left to drive.

beats.label: Boot it for real
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Secrets present, it listens on PORT — 3000 by default.” Backgrounded, so this same terminal can keep going.

verify.note: needs SLACK_BOT_TOKEN + SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET + Anthropic credentials; long-running, so it runs as job %1 the way starters/managed boots its gateway

beats.label: Count the threads it remembers
beats.cue: [manual] @-mention it in a thread, reply, then look: one session file per thread, sess_<16hex>.

verify.note: a real Slack workspace has to send the message first; sessions only exist after a live turn. The daemon is backgrounded, so this prompt is free — its log lines interleave

beats.label: Stop the daemon
beats.cue: [needs-key] Take's over — kill the backgrounded daemon before the last beats.

verify.note: job %1 is the daemon the run-boot beat backgrounded; a fresh shell has no such job

groups.title: One more thing · the Slack app setup is a command too

beats.label: Generate the Slack app manifest
beats.cue: “channel provision derives the manifest and the install steps — dry-run prints them.”

verify.note: dry run prints the app manifest YAML + the 4 install steps; writes nothing

beats.label: Preview the scope doctor
beats.cue: “Exactly which call it would make, and which scopes it would compare — before you own an app.”

verify.note: prints the would-POST auth.test plan; no network

beats.label: Run the scope doctor for real
beats.cue: [needs-key] Live auth.test plus the granted scopes — exit 1 the moment one is missing.

verify.note: hits slack.com with $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN; exits 1 on missing scopes
